title: Evaluation of modern, accelerated, and artifact-robust MRI techniques, including AI-assisted methods for whole-body imaging
summary:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides detailed images of tissue based on the magnetic properties of hydrogen atoms. Different diagnostic information can be obtained using various imaging sequences. However, due to the relatively long scan times, MRI is susceptible to image artifacts, particularly those caused by movements such as breathing or the heartbeat.

Current research aims to speed up MRI examinations, improve image quality, and reduce susceptibility to artifacts. To this end, new sequencing and reconstruction methods, as well as automated image analysis techniques, are being developed.

The goal of this research project is to evaluate such novel MRI techniques in terms of image quality, robustness, and diagnostic utility. To this end, MRI examinations are conducted on healthy volunteers and appropriate patient groups. In particular, the study examines the optimal parameterization of the methods, their image quality compared to standard methods, and their suitability for various clinical applications.

interventions.name:
Healthy adults and outpatients with a clinical indication for an MRI will be prospectively and consecutively recruited and enrolled.

Only adults will be included in the study.
Only German- or English-speaking participants will be recruited.

Exclusion criteria:
Both healthy participants and patients:
• Contraindications for MRI
• Pregnancy/breastfeeding
• Claustrophobia
• Lack of consent to disclose incidental findings
